newsitem.title: JAPAN: KDD says won't join NTT unit phone standard effort.
newsitem.headline: KDD says won't join NTT unit phone standard effort.

text.p: Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd president Tadashi Nishimoto said on Thursday that KDD would not join Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp cellular unit NTT DoCoMo's effort to develop a next generation cellular phone standard using wide band CDMA technology.
"KDD is engaged in the development of its own technology and we have no plans to join NTT DoCoMo's efforts," Nishimoto told a news conference.
"Our business will be at a disadvantage if we adopt the same standard as NTT DoCoMo."
Asked about the impact of Japan's planned deregulation of leased lines in December, Nishimoto said: "We can fully compete with our rivals if a level playing field is secured."
The Japanese government currently imposes stricter rules on the setting of rates for KDD and other telecom firms that own facilities in Japan than for those that do not own infrastructure.
KDD also announced that it has formed a wholly owned telecom consulting company in Shanghai with a total investment of $1 million.
The unit, which will support construction of telecom networks, aims for 200 million yen in sales in five years' time.
